description: What init() accepts and what it refuses, with the diagnostic code it reports.

suites.description: A sound payload loads with no error and no warning.
A file that is not an LSDE blueprint is refused outright, before anything else.
A LSDE 1.6 export is refused by name rather than half-played.
A future format version is refused, and the message names the one it reads.
A well-formed header carrying no scene.
The same id twice INSIDE one scene. Across scenes it is normal.
The counter restarts per scene, so this is the normal case, not a defect.
The same scene passed twice, as when a per-scene file is loaded twice.
A wire pointing at a block that is not in the scene.
The scene names an entry it does not hold.
A scene with no entry loads; it just cannot play. Not a reason to refuse the file.
One port, two non-async targets: they are walked in turn. Nothing to report.
The same fork with the extra target marked isAsync raises nothing either.
Wires are counted off the blocks that carry them.
A scene carrying no block list loads: it just cannot play, like an empty one.
waitForBlocks naming a block outside the scene: it can never be visited.
A router, and wires whose toPort is a card id, load with no error and no warning.
Two files of one export stack their scenes behind one header.
Pieces of two different exports are refused by name.
The same file passed twice is the same scene twice.
An empty list is no data at all. C++ cannot express this case (a payload struct always exists) and its runner skips it, saying so.
